subject: Selecting a function from unmarked - Advice needed

messages.author: 31f105464e1c4bb2
messages.subject: Selecting a function from unmarked - Advice needed
parts:
Hi unmarked users,

I'm relatively new to unmarked and would greatly appreciate some advice on selecting a function to appropriately analyze my data. I have presence/absence data from small mammal trapping conducted at 4 sites in 2012 and 8 sites in 2013 (the original 4, plus 4 new sites). Each site was trapped for 3-6 nights per year, with 20 traps deployed each night. I did not give animals individual markings upon capture, so a traditional mark-recapture analysis is not possible. I would like to explore how vegetation and other environmental variables relate to small mammal abundance across years. My current thinking is to: use pcountOpen, generate candidate models for abundance, use model selection to identify which models have support, and predict abundance from the best-supported model(s). Does this sound like a logical way to proceed? 

Thanks,
Becky

messages.author: 4a15de51da4445ae
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Selecting a function from unmarked - Advice needed
parts:
hi Becky,
 There is not an obvious answer to your question.  Having only 4 or 8 sites I would say that none of the models are really appropriate if you're interest is in modeling variation among sites.  But you do have 20 traps per site and maybe there is relevant within-site information? 

Note that pcountOpen assumes a binomial sampling model for a site and the interpretation of that for your situation is unclear.   i.e., the model assumes that y = count at some site, is a binomial random variable with index N (population size) and encounter probability p. What is y exactly?  The number of detections out of 20?  In that case interpreting N as population size doesn't make sense because N is the number of detections at a fixed number of traps.

 Sorry I can't give more precise guidance right now
regards
andy
